QA-SM-004 — Home Health Compare & Star Rating Monitoring

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy establishes systematic monitoring, analysis, and response procedures for the agency's Home Health Compare publicly reported quality measures and Star Ratings at Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Home Health Compare data represents the agency's public quality profile — the information that patients, caregivers, referral sources, payers, and surveyors use to evaluate and compare the agency. Declining Star Ratings and below-average publicly reported quality measures have direct impacts on referral volume, competitive positioning, Governing Body accountability, and regulatory scrutiny. This policy ensures that the agency continuously monitors its public quality profile, understands the drivers of its ratings, and implements targeted improvement initiatives when ratings decline or fall below acceptable levels. This policy satisfies the requirements of 42 CFR § 484.65 (QAPI program data use including publicly reported measures) and supports the benchmarking requirements of QA-PI-003.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The QAPI Coordinator

The Administrator

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

All QAPI Committee members

The CFO / Revenue Cycle Director

The Governing Body

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall actively and continuously monitor all publicly reported Home Health Compare quality measures and Star Ratings, with formal analysis conducted at each quarterly release of updated data.

4.2 Home Health Compare data shall be a standing component of the QAPI Quality Indicator Dashboard per QA-PI-002, the quarterly QAPI Performance Report per QA-PG-001, and the quarterly Governing Body report per GV-GB-001.

4.3 The agency shall maintain a Star Rating target of 4 stars or higher on both the Quality of Patient Care Star Rating and the Patient Survey Star Rating, and shall develop a documented improvement plan any time either rating falls below 4 stars.

4.4 For every publicly reported quality measure on which the agency performs below the national average for 2 consecutive reporting periods, the QAPI Committee shall direct a documented corrective action plan per QA-AE-003.

4.5 The Administrator and QAPI Coordinator shall verify the accuracy of the agency's Home Health Compare data within each quarterly release window and initiate the CMS data correction process if inaccuracies are identified.

4.6 Home Health Compare performance shall be reported publicly within the agency's marketing and referral source materials only as accurately as permitted by CMS guidelines, and shall not be misrepresented.

4.7 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid.

5. Definitions

6. Procedures

6.1 Monitoring Infrastructure

6.2 Quarterly Data Review and Analysis

6.3 QAPI Committee Review and Action

6.4 Comprehensive Star Rating Improvement Plan

6.5 Governing Body Reporting

6.6 Benchmarking Integration

6.7 Escalation and Exception Handling

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance Monitoring

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 Surveyor Expectations

Surveyors will: (1) ask whether the agency monitors its publicly reported quality measures; (2) request evidence of quarterly analysis and QAPI Committee review; (3) verify the agency acts on below-average measures; (4) assess whether the Governing Body is aware of the agency's public quality profile; (5) cross-reference survey findings with publicly reported measures to assess consistency.

8.3 Common Failure Points

9. References

References: 42 CFR § 484.65; CMS Home Health Quality Reporting Program regulations and guidance; CMS Care Compare methodology documents; cross-references QA-PG-001, QA-PG-002, QA-PI-002, QA-PI-003, QA-AE-003, QA-SM-003, CL-OA-001–CL-OA-019, GV-GB-001, FN-BC-001, EN-TG-001.

10. Training Requirements

10.1 The QAPI Coordinator shall receive training on iQIES system access, CASPER report interpretation, HH QRP submission requirements, and Home Health Compare data methodology within 30 days of appointment and annually thereafter.

10.2 All QAPI Committee members shall receive annual training on Home Health Compare measure definitions, Star Rating calculation methodology, and quality improvement strategies for commonly below-average measures.

10.3 The DON and clinical supervisors shall receive annual training on the relationship between OASIS accuracy, clinical documentation quality, and publicly reported outcome measures.

10.4 Policy acknowledgment within 14 calendar days per standard.

QA-SM-005 — Policy Effectiveness Monitoring and Outcome Validation

1. Policy Header

2. Purpose

This policy requires Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. to systematically measure whether its policies are achieving their intended outcomes through defined compliance metrics, outcome indicators, and incident correlation analysis. Policies are the foundational mechanism through which the agency operationalizes regulatory requirements, best practices, and quality standards. A policy that exists in writing but does not change behavior or achieve measurable outcomes provides no quality assurance value and may create false compliance assurance. This policy ensures that the agency's policy framework is evaluated not merely for existence and acknowledgment, but for actual effectiveness — measured through outcomes data, compliance audit results, incident trends, and staff behavior indicators. This policy supports compliance with 42 CFR § 484.65 (QAPI program data-driven improvement) and the agency's enterprise policy governance framework per EN-TG-001.

3. Scope

This policy applies to:

The Compliance Officer

The QAPI Coordinator

The Administrator

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

All QAPI Committee members

All department heads and supervisors responsible for policy implementation in their domains

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a formal Policy Effectiveness Monitoring (PEM) program that evaluates whether REQUIRED and ESSENTIAL-tier policies are achieving their intended compliance and quality outcomes.

4.2 For each REQUIRED-tier policy, at least one defined outcome indicator shall be established that, when measured, provides evidence of whether the policy is being implemented as intended and achieving its stated purpose.

4.3 Policy effectiveness shall be evaluated through three complementary mechanisms: (a) compliance audit results per CO-RA-002 and CO-DC-002; (b) defined outcome indicators monitored through the QAPI Quality Indicator Dashboard per QA-PI-002; (c) incident and adverse event correlation analysis — identifying whether adverse events are linked to policy non-compliance.

4.4 Any REQUIRED-tier policy that demonstrates persistent non-compliance (below defined threshold for 2 or more consecutive audit cycles) or persistent adverse outcome correlation shall be reviewed for revision, enhanced communication, training improvement, or structural redesign.

4.5 The Policy Effectiveness Monitoring program shall be reported to the QAPI Committee semiannually and to the Governing Body annually as part of the year-end QAPI evaluation per QA-PG-002.

4.6 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid.

6. Procedures

6.2 Compliance Metric Monitoring

6.3 Outcome Indicator Monitoring

6.4 Incident Correlation Analysis

6.5 Policy Revision Triggers and Process

6.6 QAPI Committee and Governing Body Reporting

6.7 Escalation and Exception Handling

7. Documentation Requirements

8. Compliance Monitoring

8.1 How Compliance Is Measured

8.2 Surveyor Expectations

Surveyors will: (1) ask whether the agency monitors whether its policies are actually followed and effective; (2) look for evidence that the agency uses audit and outcome data to evaluate policies, not just to document them; (3) assess whether policy non-compliance is identified and addressed systematically; (4) verify that the QAPI program integrates policy compliance as a data input; (5) look for evidence that the Governing Body is aware of policy effectiveness.

8.3 Common Failure Points

10. Training Requirements

10.1 The QAPI Coordinator and Compliance Officer shall receive training on policy effectiveness measurement methodology, compliance metric design, and incident correlation analysis within 30 days of assignment.

10.2 All department heads and supervisors shall receive training on their responsibility for policy implementation in their domain and how compliance metrics are measured within 14 calendar days of policy effective date.

SUBDOMAIN: RM-ER — ENTERPRISE RISK

POLICY: RM-ER-001 — Enterprise Risk Management Program

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy establishes the comprehensive Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) program for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The ERM program provides a systematic, agency-wide approach to identifying, assessing, mitigating, monitoring, and reporting risks across all operational domains. This policy ensures that risk management is integrated into the agency's governance structure, strategic planning, and daily operations, supporting compliance with 42 CFR Part 484, OSHA requirements, state licensure standards, and OIG Compliance Program Guidance.

2. Scope

This policy applies to:

All members of the Governing Body of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.

The Agency Administrator

The Risk Manager

The Director of Nursing / Clinical Manager

The Compliance Officer

All department directors and supervisory personnel

All clinical and administrative staff responsible for identifying and reporting risks

All contracted entities performing services on behalf of the agency

This policy does not replace domain-specific risk management activities (e.g., clinical risk managed under CL domain, financial risk under FN domain) but provides the overarching governance framework within which all domain-specific risk activities operate.

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a formal Enterprise Risk Management program that provides a systematic approach to identifying, assessing, mitigating, and monitoring risks across all agency operations.

4.2 The Governing Body shall have ultimate oversight of the ERM program and shall receive quarterly risk reports from the Risk Manager, per policy GV-GB-001 §6.2.

4.3 The Risk Manager shall be designated as the agency's ERM program leader, with authority to access all operational domains for risk identification and assessment purposes.

4.4 A centralized Risk Register shall be maintained as the single authoritative source for all identified enterprise risks. The Risk Register shall be reviewed and updated no less than quarterly.

4.5 All agency personnel shall be responsible for identifying and reporting potential risks through the agency's incident reporting system per policy RM-ER-002.

4.6 The ERM program shall be integrated with the agency's QAPI program (QA-PG-001), compliance program (CO-CP-001), and financial oversight processes (FN-FP-007) to ensure coordinated risk governance.

4.7 Risk assessments shall be conducted annually at minimum, and additionally upon any significant operational change, regulatory change, adverse event, or external threat.

4.8 The Governing Body shall formally define the agency's risk appetite and risk tolerance thresholds. Risk tolerance thresholds shall be documented and reviewed annually.

4.9 Only the most current approved version of this policy shall be considered valid. Superseded versions must not be used for any operational or compliance purpose.

5. Procedures

5.1 ERM Program Structure and Governance

5.2 Risk Identification

5.3 Risk Assessment and Prioritization

5.4 Risk Mitigation Planning

5.5 Risk Monitoring and Reporting

5.6 Integration with QAPI and Compliance Programs

6. Documentation Requirements

7. Compliance Monitoring and Measurement

7.1 Compliance Indicators

7.2 Surveyor Expectations

CMS surveyors conducting a standard survey will verify:

Evidence of a structured risk management program. Surveyors will request the ERM charter, program manual, and Risk Register.

Evidence of Governing Body oversight of risk. Surveyors will review Governing Body minutes for documented risk report presentation and action.

Evidence that risks are identified, assessed, and mitigated. Surveyors will select specific risks from the Register and trace through identification, assessment, mitigation plan, and resolution.

Integration with QAPI. Surveyors will verify that risk data informs the QAPI program and that adverse event data flows into the risk management process.

Incident reporting processes. Surveyors will verify the existence and functioning of the incident reporting system per RM-ER-002.

Staff awareness. Surveyors may interview staff regarding their understanding of how to report risks and incidents.

7.3 Common Failure Points

8. Regulatory References

8.1 Federal Regulations

8.2 Cross-Referenced Agency Policies

9. Training Requirements

9.1 The Risk Manager shall receive comprehensive training on ERM methodology, risk assessment tools, and program governance within 30 calendar days of designation.

9.2 All Risk Management Committee members shall receive orientation to this policy and the ERM program within 14 calendar days of appointment.

9.3 All department directors and supervisory personnel shall receive annual training on risk identification, reporting obligations, and their role within the ERM framework.

9.4 All clinical and administrative staff shall receive annual training on incident and risk reporting per RM-ER-002, including how to access the reporting system and what constitutes a reportable event.

9.5 All personnel within scope shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix E) within 14 calendar days of the policy effective date, any revision, or new assignment.

9.6 The Risk Manager shall maintain a training completion tracking log and report any non-compliance to the Administrator within 7 calendar days of the completion deadline.

10. Version Control

10.1 This policy is maintained under the agency's enterprise policy lifecycle management system per policy EN-LC-001.

10.2 Only the most current approved version is valid. All superseded versions must be archived and marked "SUPERSEDED — NOT FOR USE."

10.3 Any substantive revision requires: (a) review and approval by the Governing Body; (b) re-acknowledgment by all in-scope personnel within 14 calendar days; (c) update to the enterprise policy index per EN-TG-001.

10.4 Non-substantive revisions may be approved by the Administrator with notification to the Governing Body at the next regular meeting.

POLICY: RM-ER-002 — Incident Reporting & Investigation

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy establishes the requirements for reporting, documenting, and investigating all incidents, near-misses, and adverse events occurring in connection with the operations of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. A robust incident reporting system is essential for identifying risks, preventing recurrence, improving patient and staff safety, and supporting compliance with 42 CFR Part 484, OSHA requirements, and state mandatory reporting obligations.

2. Scope

This policy applies to:

All employees of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. (clinical and administrative)

All contracted and per diem staff providing services on behalf of the agency

All supervisory and management personnel

All volunteers performing activities under agency direction

The Risk Manager, Administrator, Director of Nursing, and Compliance Officer

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 All employees, contractors, and volunteers of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall immediately report any incident, adverse event, near miss, or unsafe condition through the agency's incident reporting system.

4.2 The agency shall maintain a no-retaliation policy for good-faith incident reporting. No employee shall face disciplinary action for reporting an incident, per policy CO-CP-005.

4.3 Incident reports are confidential risk management documents. They shall not be filed in the patient's clinical record and shall be maintained in the risk management file.

4.4 All incidents shall be classified by severity level and investigated according to a tiered investigation protocol proportional to severity.

4.5 Mandatory external reporting obligations (to state agencies, CMS, law enforcement, adult protective services) shall be fulfilled within the timeframes required by applicable law, regardless of internal investigation status.

4.6 All sentinel events shall trigger an immediate investigation and root cause analysis per policy QA-AE-002.

4.7 Incident data shall be aggregated, trended, and reported to the Risk Management Committee quarterly per RM-ER-005, and to the QAPI Committee per QA-PG-003.

5. Procedures

5.1 Immediate Response

5.2 Incident Report Completion

5.3 Incident Classification

5.4 Investigation Process

5.5 Mandatory External Reporting

5.6 Corrective Action and Follow-Up

5.7 Trending and Analysis

6. Documentation Requirements

7. Compliance Monitoring and Measurement

Common Failure Points

8. Regulatory References

Cross-Referenced Policies

9. Training Requirements

9.1 All new employees shall receive incident reporting training during orientation, within 14 calendar days of hire, covering: (a) what constitutes a reportable incident; (b) how to complete the Incident Report Form; (c) to whom and when to report; (d) non-retaliation protections; (e) distinction between incident report and clinical documentation.

9.2 All staff shall receive annual refresher training on incident reporting.

9.3 All supervisory staff shall receive additional training on: (a) Incident Report review and completion oversight; (b) immediate response and escalation protocols; (c) evidence preservation.

9.4 The Risk Manager and Investigation Team members shall receive training on investigation methodology and root cause analysis.

9.5 All in-scope personnel shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix G) within 14 calendar days of effective date, revision, or new hire.

10. Version Control

Per RM-ER-001 §10. Only the most current approved version is valid.

POLICY: RM-ER-003 — Risk Assessment & Prioritization

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy mandates the conduct of regular, systematic risk assessments across all operational domains of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Risk assessments provide the foundation for informed decision-making, resource allocation, and risk mitigation by identifying, scoring, and prioritizing risks based on likelihood and severity of impact.

2. Scope

This policy applies to the Risk Manager, all department directors, the Administrator, the Risk Management Committee, and all personnel responsible for conducting or contributing to risk assessments.

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall conduct a comprehensive enterprise-wide risk assessment annually.

4.2 Targeted risk assessments shall be conducted within 72 hours of any triggering event as defined in RM-ER-001 §5.2.5.

4.3 All risk assessments shall use the agency's standardized Risk Assessment Matrix (RM-ER-001, Appendix A) to ensure consistency.

4.4 Department directors shall participate in the annual comprehensive risk assessment by identifying and submitting domain-specific risks.

4.5 All assessed risks shall be documented in the centralized Risk Register per RM-ER-001.

4.6 Risk prioritization shall directly inform the agency's mitigation planning, resource allocation, and strategic planning processes.

POLICY: RM-ER-004 — Liability & Insurance Management

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy establishes requirements for maintaining adequate insurance coverage as a core risk transfer strategy within the ERM framework of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Appropriate insurance coverage protects the agency, its patients, staff, and governing body from financial loss resulting from liability claims, property damage, and other insurable risks.

2. Scope

This policy applies to the Governing Body, Administrator, Risk Manager, CFO/Revenue Cycle Director, and any personnel involved in insurance procurement, claims management, or risk transfer decisions.

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain current and adequate insurance coverage as a fundamental component of its enterprise risk management strategy.

4.2 The following insurance coverage types shall be maintained at minimum:

(a) Professional liability (malpractice) insurance

(b) General liability insurance

(c) Workers' compensation insurance (per California state law)

(d) Commercial auto insurance (for agency-owned or leased vehicles, if applicable)

(e) Cyber liability insurance

(f) Directors & Officers liability insurance (if the Governing Body includes a board of directors)

4.3 Coverage levels shall be reviewed annually by the Risk Manager and Administrator to ensure adequacy based on current risk exposure, agency size, service volume, and industry benchmarks.

4.4 The Governing Body shall approve insurance coverage levels annually as part of the budget approval process per FN-FP-005.

4.5 No lapse in required insurance coverage shall occur. The Risk Manager shall monitor all policy expiration dates and initiate renewal no later than 90 calendar days before expiration.

4.6 All contracted and per diem staff shall provide evidence of current professional liability insurance coverage prior to providing services per HR-WM-002.

5. Procedures

5.1 Insurance Program Management

5.2 Contractor Insurance Verification

5.3 Claims Notification and Management

6. Documentation Requirements

7. Compliance Monitoring and Measurement

8. Regulatory References

Cross-Referenced Policies

9. Training Requirements

9.1 The Risk Manager shall maintain current knowledge of insurance products, claims management, and liability risk mitigation.

9.2 The Administrator and CFO shall receive annual briefing on insurance coverage, claims status, and adequacy review findings.

9.3 All in-scope personnel shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix D) within 14 calendar days.

10. Version Control

Per RM-ER-001 §10.

POLICY: RM-ER-005 — Risk Trending & Pattern Analysis

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy mandates systematic analysis of risk, incident, and adverse event data to identify trends, patterns, and systemic issues requiring proactive intervention. Trending and pattern analysis transforms raw data into actionable intelligence that supports evidence-based risk mitigation and quality improvement.

2. Scope

This policy applies to the Risk Manager, QAPI Coordinator, Risk Management Committee, and all personnel who generate, collect, or analyze risk-related data.

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 The Risk Manager shall conduct monthly trending analysis of all incident and risk data.

4.2 Quarterly trending reports shall be presented to the Risk Management Committee, QAPI Committee, and Governing Body per RM-ER-001.

4.3 Any identified cluster (3+ similar events within 30 days) shall trigger an immediate investigation and escalation per §5.3.

4.4 Trending data shall directly inform risk assessment priorities, mitigation planning, training needs identification, and QAPI project selection.

4.5 Both leading and lagging indicators shall be monitored to enable proactive risk mitigation.

5. Procedures

5.1 Data Collection and Aggregation

5.2 Trending Analysis

5.3 Cluster Identification and Escalation

5.4 Reporting and Integration

6. Documentation Requirements

7. Compliance Monitoring and Measurement

8. Regulatory References and Cross-Referenced Policies

POLICY: RM-ER-006 — Claims Management & Litigation Support

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy establishes procedures for managing liability claims, coordinating with legal counsel, preserving evidence, and supporting litigation defense for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Effective claims management minimizes financial exposure, protects the agency's reputation, and ensures compliance with legal and insurance requirements.

2. Scope

This policy applies to the Risk Manager, Administrator, Compliance Officer, Governing Body, legal counsel, insurance carriers, and any personnel involved in claims-related activities or litigation support.

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 All claims, demand letters, lawsuits, subpoenas, and notices of potential claims received by any agency employee shall be immediately forwarded to the Risk Manager.

4.2 The Risk Manager shall notify the applicable insurance carrier(s) within 24 hours of receiving any claim or notice of potential claim per RM-ER-004.

4.3 A litigation hold shall be issued within 24 hours of receiving any lawsuit, demand letter, or credible notice of potential litigation.

4.4 No agency employee shall discuss claims, litigation, or potential litigation with any external party (including claimants, their attorneys, or media) without authorization from the Risk Manager or legal counsel.

4.5 The Governing Body shall be notified of all claims and lawsuits per GV-GB-001 §6.5.

4.6 All claims management activities shall be coordinated with the agency's legal counsel per GV-EA-003.

5. Procedures

5.1 Claims Receipt and Initial Response

5.2 Litigation Hold and Evidence Preservation

5.3 Claims Investigation and Coordination

5.4 Resolution and Closure

6. Documentation Requirements

7. Compliance Monitoring and Measurement

8. Regulatory References and Cross-Referenced Policies

9. Training Requirements

9.1 All agency employees shall receive training during orientation on: (a) the obligation to immediately forward any claim or legal document to the Risk Manager; (b) the prohibition against discussing claims with external parties.

9.2 All supervisory personnel shall receive additional training on evidence preservation and litigation hold procedures.

9.3 All in-scope personnel shall sign Appendix C within 14 calendar days.

10. Version Control

Per RM-ER-001 §10.

SUBDOMAIN: RM-SS — STAFF SAFETY

POLICY: RM-SS-001 — Staff Safety & Personal Security

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy defines protocols for staff safety during home visits, including threat assessment, communication check-ins, and high-risk visit procedures for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. The safety of staff providing services in uncontrolled home environments is paramount and requires proactive safety planning, clear communication protocols, and immediate response capabilities.

2. Scope

This policy applies to all employees, contracted staff, and per diem personnel of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. who provide services in patient homes or travel for agency business, as well as supervisory personnel responsible for staff deployment and scheduling.

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a comprehensive staff safety program that protects all personnel during home health visits and agency travel.

4.2 A Home Visit Safety Assessment shall be conducted for every new patient prior to or at the time of the first visit, and updated whenever safety conditions change.

4.3 All field staff shall follow the agency's Check-In Protocol during patient visits. No staff member shall make a home visit without notifying the agency of their location and expected return.

4.4 Visits shall not be conducted when the staff member's safety is in imminent danger. Staff have the right and obligation to leave a home immediately if they feel unsafe.

4.5 High-risk visits shall require enhanced safety measures including the buddy system, specific check-in intervals, and supervisor notification.

4.6 All staff shall receive initial and annual training on personal safety, de-escalation techniques, and emergency response procedures.

4.7 All safety incidents involving staff shall be reported per RM-ER-002 and investigated.

5. Procedures

5.1 Home Visit Safety Assessment

5.2 Check-In Protocol

5.3 High-Risk Visit Procedures

5.4 Duress Communication

5.5 Post-Incident Response

6. Documentation Requirements

7. Compliance Monitoring and Measurement

Common Failure Points

8. Regulatory References

Cross-Referenced Policies

9. Training Requirements

9.1 All field staff shall receive initial safety training within 14 calendar days of hire covering: (a) Home Visit Safety Assessment; (b) Check-In Protocol; (c) High-Risk Visit procedures; (d) Duress code and Safe Zone; (e) De-escalation techniques; (f) Right to leave unsafe situations; (g) Incident reporting.

9.2 Annual refresher training shall be provided to all field staff.

9.3 All in-scope personnel shall sign Appendix C within 14 calendar days.

10. Version Control

POLICY: RM-SS-002 — Workplace Violence Prevention

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy establishes Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc.'s workplace violence prevention program, including risk assessment, reporting protocols, response procedures, and staff protection measures. Home health workers face elevated violence risk due to the uncontrolled home environment, and this policy provides a comprehensive prevention and response framework in compliance with Cal/OSHA workplace violence prevention standards (SB 553).

2. Scope

This policy applies to all employees, contractors, per diem staff, and volunteers of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. It covers all work settings including patient homes, the agency office, community locations, and while in transit.

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. maintains a zero-tolerance policy for workplace violence. No acts of violence, threats, intimidation, harassment, or bullying will be tolerated from any person — employee, patient, family member, visitor, or third party.

4.2 All staff shall immediately report any incident of workplace violence, threat, or intimidation per RM-ER-002 and this policy.

4.3 No employee shall be retaliated against for reporting workplace violence in good faith, per CO-CP-005.

4.4 The agency shall maintain a written Workplace Violence Prevention Plan (WVPP) as required by California SB 553, effective July 1, 2024.

4.5 Threat assessments shall be conducted for all reported credible threats by the Risk Manager within 24 hours.

4.6 All staff shall receive initial and annual workplace violence prevention training.

5. Procedures

5.2 Incident Reporting and Response

5.3 Investigation and Follow-Up

POLICY: RM-SS-003 — Motor Vehicle Safety & Accident Reporting

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy establishes standards for motor vehicle safety, driving eligibility, accident reporting, and investigation procedures for all personnel of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. who operate motor vehicles for agency business. Home health services require extensive driving in variable conditions, and motor vehicle accidents represent a significant risk to staff safety, patient service continuity, agency liability, and insurance costs.

2. Scope

This policy applies to:

All employees of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. who use personal vehicles or agency-owned/leased vehicles for agency business

All contracted and per diem staff who drive to patient homes or other locations for agency services

All supervisory and management personnel responsible for staff deployment

The Risk Manager, HR Director, and Administrator

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 All personnel who drive for agency business shall maintain a valid driver's license appropriate for the vehicle operated and carry minimum automobile insurance coverage as required by California state law.

4.2 The agency shall verify the motor vehicle record (MVR) of all personnel who drive for agency business at the time of hire and annually thereafter.

4.3 All motor vehicle accidents occurring during agency business shall be reported immediately per the procedures in this policy and documented per RM-ER-002.

4.4 The use of handheld electronic devices while operating a motor vehicle for agency business is strictly prohibited, consistent with California Vehicle Code § 23123 and § 23123.5.

4.5 All personnel shall comply with all applicable traffic laws, wear seatbelts at all times, and operate vehicles in a safe and defensive manner.

4.6 Personnel who fail to maintain driving eligibility or who demonstrate unsafe driving practices shall be restricted from driving for agency business.

4.7 Agency-owned or leased vehicles (if applicable) shall be maintained in safe operating condition with documented maintenance records.

5. Procedures

5.1 Driving Eligibility and Verification

5.2 Safe Driving Standards

5.3 Motor Vehicle Accident Response

5.4 Accident Investigation

5.5 Agency Vehicle Management (If Applicable)

6. Documentation Requirements

7. Compliance Monitoring and Measurement

7.1 Compliance Indicators

7.2 Surveyor Expectations

CMS surveyors may review staff safety measures including transportation safety during survey of 42 CFR § 484.105 (organization and administration). Surveyors will verify:

Evidence that the agency has established vehicle safety standards for staff

Evidence of training on safe driving practices

Evidence that motor vehicle accidents are reported, investigated, and trended

Integration of motor vehicle accident data into the agency's QAPI and risk management programs

7.3 Common Failure Points

8. Regulatory References

Cross-Referenced Policies

9. Training Requirements

9.1 All personnel who drive for agency business shall receive motor vehicle safety training within 14 calendar days of hire covering: (a) safe driving standards; (b) pre-trip vehicle inspection; (c) distracted driving prohibition; (d) accident response procedures; (e) reporting requirements; (f) obligation to report license/insurance changes.

9.2 Annual refresher training shall be provided to all driving staff.

9.3 Additional remedial driving safety training shall be required for any employee involved in a preventable accident.

9.4 All in-scope personnel shall sign the Policy Acknowledgment Form (Appendix D) within 14 calendar days.

SUBDOMAIN: RM-PS — PATIENT & ENVIRONMENTAL SAFETY

POLICY: RM-PS-001 — Environmental Safety Assessment

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy establishes requirements for assessing and documenting the home environment for safety hazards that may affect patient health, safety, and clinical outcomes for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Home health services are delivered in uncontrolled environments where hazards—including structural deficiencies, fire risks, infection risks, fall hazards, and environmental contaminants—may compromise patient and staff safety. Systematic environmental assessment enables identification, documentation, patient/caregiver education, and mitigation of hazards to the extent possible.

2. Scope

This policy applies to all clinical staff of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. who provide services in patient homes, including registered nurses, licensed vocational nurses, physical therapists, occupational therapists, speech-language pathologists, medical social workers, home health aides, and their supervisors.

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 An Environmental Safety Assessment shall be completed for every patient at the time of admission (SOC/ROC) and documented in the clinical record.

4.2 Environmental safety shall be reassessed at each recertification, upon any reported change in the home environment, upon any safety incident, and as clinically indicated.

4.3 All identified hazards shall be documented, discussed with the patient/caregiver, and addressed through education, intervention, or referral to the extent possible.

4.4 If a hazard cannot be mitigated and creates an imminent risk to patient safety, the clinician shall notify the supervisor immediately and the agency shall determine whether services can safely continue.

4.5 Environmental Safety Assessment findings shall be communicated to all disciplines providing care in the home.

4.6 Environmental safety data shall be aggregated and reported to the QAPI Committee and Risk Management Committee quarterly for trending analysis.

5. Procedures

5.1 Initial Environmental Safety Assessment

5.2 Ongoing Environmental Safety Monitoring

5.3 Environmental Safety Referrals

5.4 Data Aggregation and Reporting

6. Documentation Requirements

7. Compliance Monitoring and Measurement

Common Failure Points

8. Regulatory References

Cross-Referenced Policies

9. Training Requirements

9.1 All clinical staff shall receive training on environmental safety assessment during orientation within 14 calendar days of hire.

9.2 Annual refresher training on environmental safety assessment, including common hazards, documentation requirements, and escalation procedures.

9.3 All in-scope personnel shall sign Appendix C within 14 calendar days.

10. Version Control

Per RM-ER-001 §10.

POLICY: RM-PS-002 — Hazardous Materials & Waste Management

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy defines procedures for the safe handling, storage, transport, and disposal of biohazardous materials, sharps, pharmaceutical waste, and other regulated medical waste generated during home health service delivery by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Compliance with OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard, California Medical Waste Management Act, and EPA regulations is required to protect staff, patients, and the community.

2. Scope

This policy applies to all clinical staff, home health aides, and any personnel who handle, transport, or dispose of medical waste, sharps, biohazardous materials, or pharmaceutical waste during agency operations.

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 All staff shall follow Standard Precautions when handling blood, body fluids, or other potentially infectious materials per CL-SD-016 and OSHA 29 CFR § 1910.1030.

4.2 Sharps shall be disposed of immediately after use in an approved sharps container at the point of use. Recapping of needles is prohibited.

4.3 Biohazardous waste generated in the patient's home shall be managed and disposed of in compliance with California Medical Waste Management Act (Health & Safety Code § 117600 et seq.) and agency procedures.

4.4 All staff shall have access to appropriate PPE and shall be trained on its proper use, removal, and disposal.

4.5 Exposure incidents shall be reported and managed per the agency's Exposure Control Plan and RM-ER-002.

4.6 Pharmaceutical waste shall be disposed of per FDA and EPA guidelines, with controlled substances disposed of per DEA requirements.

5. Procedures

5.1 Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)

5.2 Sharps Management

5.3 Biohazardous Waste Management

5.4 Pharmaceutical Waste Disposal

5.5 Exposure Incident Response

6. Documentation Requirements

7. Compliance Monitoring and Measurement

Common Failure Points

8. Regulatory References

Cross-Referenced Policies

9. Training Requirements

9.1 All clinical staff shall receive Bloodborne Pathogens training within 14 calendar days of hire and annually thereafter per OSHA 29 CFR § 1910.1030(g)(2).

9.2 Training shall cover: (a) OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard; (b) agency Exposure Control Plan; (c) PPE selection, use, removal, and disposal; (d) sharps safety; (e) biohazardous waste handling; (f) pharmaceutical waste disposal; (g) exposure incident response; (h) Hepatitis B vaccination availability.

9.3 All in-scope personnel shall sign Appendix C within 14 calendar days.

POLICY: RM-PS-003 — Product & Equipment Safety Recall Management

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy defines procedures for monitoring, responding to, and documenting medical product, medical device, and equipment safety recalls and alerts affecting patients or operations of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Timely identification and response to recalls protects patients from harm due to defective products and ensures regulatory compliance.

2. Scope

This policy applies to the Risk Manager, Operations Director, Director of Nursing, all clinical staff, and all personnel responsible for procuring, distributing, or using medical products, devices, or equipment on behalf of the agency.

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 The Risk Manager shall monitor FDA recall and safety alert databases weekly to identify recalls that may affect agency operations or patients.

4.2 Upon identification of a recall affecting agency products or patient-in-use products, the agency shall respond according to the recall classification and urgency per the procedures in this policy.

4.3 All Class I recalls affecting products in agency possession or patient use shall be treated as emergent and responded to within 24 hours.

4.4 All recall actions shall be documented in the Recall Tracking Log (Appendix A) and retained for a minimum of 7 years.

4.5 Products subject to recall shall be immediately removed from use, segregated, and labeled "DO NOT USE — RECALL" pending disposition per manufacturer/FDA instructions.

POLICY: RM-PS-004 — Patient Elopement & Wandering Risk

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy defines risk assessment and intervention protocols for patients at risk of elopement or unsafe wandering served by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Patients with cognitive impairment, dementia, delirium, behavioral health conditions, or developmental disabilities may be at risk of leaving their home environment unsafely, resulting in injury, exposure, or death. Systematic identification, documentation, and care planning reduce this risk.

2. Scope

This policy applies to all clinical staff who assess, plan, and deliver care to patients with identified or suspected elopement/wandering risk, their supervisors, and the Director of Nursing.

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 All patients shall be screened for elopement/wandering risk at SOC/ROC as part of the comprehensive assessment.

4.2 Patients identified as at risk shall have an individualized Wandering/Elopement Safety Plan documented in the plan of care.

4.3 Caregivers of at-risk patients shall be educated on elopement prevention strategies, monitoring techniques, and emergency response.

4.4 Elopement events shall be reported per RM-ER-002 and investigated.

4.5 The agency shall not physically restrain patients per CL-PR-004 but shall implement environmental, educational, and monitoring interventions.

5. Procedures

5.1 Elopement/Wandering Risk Screening

5.2 Safety Plan Development

5.3 Ongoing Monitoring

5.4 Elopement Event Response

6. Documentation Requirements

7. Compliance Monitoring and Measurement

8. Regulatory References and Cross-Referenced Policies

9. Training Requirements

9.1 All clinical staff shall receive training on elopement/wandering risk identification during orientation.

9.2 Annual refresher training for all clinical staff.

9.3 All in-scope personnel shall sign Appendix C within 14 calendar days.

10. Version Control

Per RM-ER-001 §10.

POLICY: RM-PS-005 — High-Risk Medication Safety

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy establishes enhanced safety protocols for the management of high-risk medications in the home health setting by Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. High-risk medications, including anticoagulants, opioids, insulin, and other agents with narrow therapeutic indices, carry an elevated potential for serious harm if not properly managed. This policy ensures patient safety through structured assessment, monitoring, education, and coordination.

2. Scope

This policy applies to all clinical staff who assess, administer, manage, or educate patients regarding high-risk medications, including registered nurses, licensed vocational nurses, therapists contributing to medication management, and their supervisors.

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 The agency shall maintain a list of designated high-risk/high-alert medications based on the ISMP List of High-Alert Medications in Community/Ambulatory Settings, updated annually.

4.2 Enhanced safety protocols shall be applied to all patients receiving high-risk medications, including increased assessment frequency, structured monitoring parameters, patient/caregiver education, and documented safety checks.

4.3 All medication adverse events involving high-risk medications shall be reported per RM-ER-002 and QA-AE-001.

4.4 The agency shall maintain competency requirements for all clinical staff involved in high-risk medication management.

4.5 High-risk medication safety data shall be monitored and reported to the QAPI Committee quarterly.

5. Procedures

5.1 High-Risk Medication Identification

5.2 Enhanced Assessment and Monitoring

5.3 Medication-Specific Protocols

5.4 Patient/Caregiver Education

5.5 Adverse Event Response

6. Documentation Requirements

7. Compliance Monitoring and Measurement

Common Failure Points

8. Regulatory References

Cross-Referenced Policies

9. Training Requirements

9.1 All clinical staff shall receive training on high-risk medication safety during orientation within 14 calendar days of hire.

9.2 Annual competency evaluation for all clinical staff on high-risk medication management, including medication-specific protocols for anticoagulants, opioids, insulin, and digoxin.

9.3 All in-scope personnel shall sign Appendix D within 14 calendar days.

10. Version Control

Per RM-ER-001 §10.

SUBDOMAIN: RM-EP — EMERGENCY & PANDEMIC RESPONSE

POLICY: RM-EP-001 — Pandemic & Infectious Disease Response

Policy Header

1. Purpose

This policy establishes the agency's response framework for pandemic and infectious disease outbreaks including staff protection, patient triage, service modification protocols, and coordination with public health authorities for Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. Pandemics and infectious disease outbreaks require rapid, coordinated, and sustained response to protect staff and patients while maintaining essential services.

2. Scope

This policy applies to all employees, contractors, per diem staff, and volunteers of Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. It is activated by the Administrator upon declaration of a public health emergency by federal, state, or local authorities, or upon determination by the agency that an infectious disease outbreak poses a significant risk to staff or patients.

3. Definitions

4. Policy Statements

4.1 Care Indeed Home Health Care, Inc. shall maintain a Pandemic Response Plan that addresses preparation, response, and recovery phases.

4.2 The agency shall maintain a minimum 30-day supply of critical PPE at all times.

4.3 Staff protection shall be prioritized, including PPE provision, exposure protocols, and accommodation for high-risk staff.

4.4 Service delivery shall be modified as necessary during a pandemic to balance patient safety, staff safety, and essential service continuity.

4.5 The agency shall coordinate with local, state, and federal public health authorities during any outbreak or pandemic.

4.6 All pandemic response activities shall be documented and debriefed following event resolution.

5. Procedures

5.1 Preparedness

5.2 Activation and Response

5.3 Infection Control During Response

5.4 Deactivation and Recovery

6. Documentation Requirements

7. Compliance Monitoring and Measurement

8. Regulatory References

Cross-Referenced Policies

9. Training Requirements

9.1 All staff shall receive training on the Pandemic Response Plan during orientation.

9.2 Annual refresher training including infection control, PPE use, and pandemic response procedures.

9.3 Additional just-in-time training provided at activation addressing the specific pathogen and response protocols.

9.4 All in-scope personnel shall sign Appendix C within 14 calendar days.

10. Version Control

Per RM-ER-001 §10.

## Gold Standard Format Reference (GV-GB-001)

All policies should match this section structure:

| Order | Level | Title | Tab | Required |
| ----: | ----: | :---- | :-- | :------: |
| 1 | 1 | `{Policy Title}` | (cover) | ✓ |
| 2 | 2 | `1\. Policy Header` | Overview | ✓ |
| 3 | 2 | `2\. Purpose` | Overview | ✓ |
| 4 | 2 | `3\. Scope` | Overview | ✓ |
| 5 | 2 | `4\. Policy Statement` | Overview | ✓ |
| 6 | 2 | `5\. Definitions` | Overview | ✓ |
| 7 | 2 | `6\. Procedures` | Procedures | ✓ |
| 19 | 2 | `7\. Documentation Requirements` | Documentation | ○ |

## Gold Standard Format Reference (GV-GB-001)

All policies should match this section structure:

| Order | Level | Title | Tab | Required |
| ----: | ----: | :---- | :-- | :------: |
| 1 | 1 | `{Policy Title}` | (cover) | ✓ |
| 2 | 2 | `1\. Policy Header` | Overview | ✓ |
| 3 | 2 | `2\. Purpose` | Overview | ✓ |
| 4 | 2 | `3\. Scope` | Overview | ✓ |
| 5 | 2 | `4\. Policy Statement` | Overview | ✓ |
| 6 | 2 | `5\. Definitions` | Overview | ✓ |
| 7 | 2 | `6\. Procedures` | Procedures | ✓ |
| 19 | 2 | `7\. Documentation Requirements` | Documentation | ○ |

## Policies/QA-VBP-101 - HHVBP Performance & Outcomes Management.md

# POLICY QA-VBP-101 — HHVBP PERFORMANCE & OUTCOMES MANAGEMENT

| Field | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Policy ID | QA-VBP-101 |
| Policy Title | HHVBP Performance & Outcomes Management |
| Domain | QA — Quality Assurance & Performance Improvement |
| Subdomain | VBP — Value-Based Purchasing |
| Classification Tier | REQUIRED |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Effective Date | 2026-04-29 |
| Status | ACTIVE |
| Review Cycle | Annual |
| Access Tier | Tier 2 — Restricted |
| Policy Owner / Steward | QAPI Director |
| Approved By | Governing Body Chair |
| Regulatory Tags | HHVBP, HHQRP, 42 CFR § 484.65, 42 CFR § 484.245, 42 CFR § 484.345 |

---

## 1. PURPOSE

This policy operationalizes the agency's compliance with the expanded Home Health Value-Based Purchasing (HHVBP) Model under 42 CFR Part 484, Subpart F, integrating performance measurement, monitoring, corrective action, and reimbursement-impact governance with the QAPI program (QA-PG-001/002). It ensures that every measure component contributing to the agency's Total Performance Score (TPS) — OASIS-based, claims-based, and HHCAHPS — is monitored, defended with evidence, and actively improved.

---

## 2. SCOPE

Applies to all clinical, administrative, billing, and patient-experience operations contributing to HHVBP-impacting measures, including but not limited to: TNC Self-Care, TNC Mobility, Discharged to Community, Acute Care Hospitalization (ACH) within first 60 days, Emergency Department Use without Hospitalization (ED Use), HHCAHPS composite measures, and any future CMS-published HHVBP measure.

---

## 3. POLICY STATEMENTS

3.1 The agency shall maintain an HHVBP Performance Program that monitors all CMS-published HHVBP measures monthly using interim Care Compare and HHVBP iQIES Performance Reports.

3.2 Patient experience (HHCAHPS) shall be monitored using the contracted CAHPS vendor's monthly composite reports and integrated into QAPI per QA-PG-002.

3.3 Performance score thresholds shall trigger mandatory corrective action: (a) any measure dropping ≥ 10 percentile points quarter-over-quarter; (b) any measure below the cohort 25th percentile for two consecutive quarters; (c) projected TPS in the bottom payment-adjustment band.

3.4 HHVBP performance shall be a standing agenda item at QAPI Committee (monthly), Compliance Committee (quarterly), and Governing Body (quarterly) meetings.

3.5 Reimbursement-impact projections (estimated payment adjustment based on rolling TPS) shall be calculated quarterly by Finance in coordination with QAPI and reported to the Governing Body.

3.6 Clinical Improvement Plans (CIPs) for under-performing measures shall be developed using PDSA methodology, assigned an accountable owner, and tracked to closure with evidence.

3.7 Underlying data integrity (OASIS, claims, HHCAHPS) shall be governed by CL-OA-101, CL-DC-101, and the agency's billing accuracy program (CO-FW-101 §6.1.3).

3.8 **Workflow Enforcement & Evidence Clause (Mandatory).** Execution of this policy shall generate auditable evidence within the system. All actions must be recorded with `policy_id`, `workflow_id`, and `event_id`. Actions not supported by system-generated evidence shall be considered non-compliant.

---

## 4. DEFINITIONS

| Term | Definition |
| :---- | :---- |
| HHVBP | Home Health Value-Based Purchasing Model — CMS payment model adjusting Medicare fee-for-service payments based on quality performance. |
| TPS | Total Performance Score — composite weighted score across HHVBP measures driving the annual payment adjustment. |
| Achievement Threshold | The median of national performance during the baseline year for a measure. |
| Benchmark | The mean of the top decile of national performance during the baseline year. |
| HHCAHPS | Home Health Consumer Assessment of Healthcare Providers and Systems — patient experience survey. |
| Clinical Improvement Plan (CIP) | A QAPI-aligned, PDSA-structured plan to improve a specific measure. |

---

## 5. PROCEDURES

### 5.1 Measure Monitoring

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 5.1.1 | QAPI Director | Pull monthly HHVBP iQIES Performance Report and Care Compare measure refresh; reconcile with internal claims/OASIS extracts. | Monthly. |
| 5.1.2 | QAPI Director | Update HHVBP Dashboard (achievement / improvement / TPS projection) and post to QAPI Committee. (`event_id = vbp.dashboard.publish`). | Monthly. |
| 5.1.3 | CAHPS Vendor + QAPI | Receive HHCAHPS composite data; integrate into dashboard. | Monthly. |

### 5.2 Threshold Detection & Corrective Action

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 5.2.1 | QAPI Director | On threshold breach (§3.3), open a Clinical Improvement Plan (`workflow_id = vbp.cip.open`). | Within 7 calendar days. |
| 5.2.2 | CIP Owner | Conduct PDSA cycle; capture interventions, metrics, and outcome evidence. | Initial PDSA in 30 days. |
| 5.2.3 | QAPI Committee | Review CIP progress monthly until measure stabilizes ≥ achievement threshold. | Monthly. |

### 5.3 Reimbursement Impact

| Step | Responsible Party | Action | Timeframe |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 5.3.1 | CFO + QAPI Director | Calculate projected payment adjustment using current rolling TPS. | Quarterly. |
| 5.3.2 | CFO | Report projected impact to Governing Body. | Quarterly. |

### 5.4 Data Integrity Linkage

OASIS-based measures depend on CL-OA-101 audit results; claims-based measures depend on CO-FW-101 §6.1.3 billing audits; HHCAHPS depends on patient roster accuracy and survey vendor controls. Any data-integrity finding shall pause CIP closure until the root cause is corrected.

---

## 6. EVIDENCE & TRACEABILITY (per EN-WF-101)

All HHVBP monitoring, CIP, and reporting events persist to the Evidence Repository with `policy_id = QA-VBP-101`, `workflow_id`, `event_id`, `measure_id`, `period`, `score_value`, `cohort_percentile`, `tps_projection`, `user_id`, and `timestamp`.

---

## 7. DOCUMENTATION & RETENTION

| Record | Retention |
| :---- | :---- |
| Monthly HHVBP dashboards | 7 years |
| CIP records (charter, PDSA logs, closure) | 7 years |
| HHCAHPS vendor reports | 7 years |
| Governing Body minutes referencing TPS | Permanent (per GV-GB-001) |
| Reimbursement impact analyses | 7 years |

---

## 8. COMPLIANCE MEASUREMENT

| Indicator | Target |
| :---- | :---- |
| Monthly HHVBP dashboard published | 100% on time |
| CIPs opened within 7 days of breach | 100% |
| Measures meeting/exceeding achievement threshold | ≥ 70% |
| Projected TPS payment adjustment band | Neutral or positive |
| HHCAHPS response rate | ≥ national median |

---

## 9. REGULATORY REFERENCES

- 42 CFR Part 484, Subpart F — Expanded HHVBP Model
- 42 CFR § 484.65 — QAPI
- 42 CFR § 484.245 — Reporting and Public Reporting (HHQRP)
- CY 2024–2026 HH PPS Final Rules (HHVBP measure set updates)
- HHVBP Technical Specifications (current)
- HHCAHPS Protocols and Guidelines Manual

### Cross-Referenced Policies
QA-PG-001, QA-PG-002, QA-AE-003, QA-SM-004, CL-OA-101, CL-DC-101, CL-CC-101, CO-FW-101, EN-WF-101, GV-GB-001, FN-FP-007.

---

## 10. TRAINING

QAPI staff: HHVBP measure-specification training annually. Field clinicians: 60-minute HHVBP-impact orientation at hire and annually, emphasizing the patient-experience and outcome chain.

---

## 11. CHANGELOG

| Version | Date | Author | Summary |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1.0 | 2026-04-29 | QAPI Director | Initial release. Establishes HHVBP performance program, threshold-based CIP triggers, reimbursement-impact reporting, and full evidence traceability per EN-WF-101. |

## 3. DETAILED FINDINGS (INITIAL PASS ONLY)

### Critical Findings — Meeting Minutes

1. **GV — Administrator Appointment (GV-WF-03):** Previously verified compliant; GV-FM-005 present. User feedback triggered systemic audit — no defect here.
2. **FN — Annual Operating Budget (FN-WF-01):** Cited `GV-FM-011` (Governing Body Roster) incorrectly as "Committee Charter & Meeting Minutes." **Corrected** to `FN-FM-014 Finance Committee Meeting Minutes` (newly created) + `GV-FM-005` for Board acknowledgment.
3. **FN — Denials / AR / Bad Debt (FN-WF-09):** Same mis-cite. **Corrected** identically.
4. **HR — Licensure & Credentialing (HR-WF-04):** Cited `GV-FM-010` (Legal Counsel Engagement Authorization) instead of licensure tracker. **Corrected** to `GV-FM-019 Agency Licensure & Certification Tracking Log`; added `GV-FM-005`.
5. **FN / HR / EN Workflows — `CO-FM-003` misuse:** `CO-FM-003` (Compliance Hotline Submission) was referenced as "Compliance Committee Meeting Minutes" in 11 places. **Corrected** to `CO-FM-024 Compliance Committee Meeting Minutes` globally.
6. **Multiple Domains — Missing GV-FM-005 at Board-reporting steps:** Workflows in IT, HR, OP, CL, FN, RM, EN referenced "Board briefing" or "Report to Governing Body" but listed only `GV-FM-023` (Annual Compliance Report). **Corrected** by adding `GV-FM-005` in step, required forms, outputs, and audit requirements.

### Critical Findings — Missing Forms

7. **Committee Minutes Gap:** No dedicated forms existed for Finance Committee, Audit Committee, Risk Committee, Safety Committee (IIPP/SB 553), IT/Security Committee, or Change Advisory Board. **Created** FN-FM-014, FN-FM-015, RM-FM-017, RM-FM-018, IT-FM-031, IT-FM-038. Each is portrait-oriented, audit_critical, master_template classification, with full attendees/quorum/motions/recommendations-to-GB/signature blocks aligned with GV-FM-005 format.
8. **Legal Hold / Records Destruction:** No forms existed for legal-hold issuance or records-destruction authorization. **Created** EN-FM-030 Legal Hold Notice and EN-FM-031 Records Destruction Authorization.
9. **Post-Incident CAP (IT/Security):** No dedicated IT corrective-action form existed. **Created** IT-FM-032 Post-Incident Corrective Action Plan (IT/Security).
10. **Enterprise Mandatory Events / KPI / Management Review / Attestation / Certification:** Workflow references existed for EN-FM-025…030 but names did not match intent. **Created** EN-FM-032 (Mandatory Events Calendar), EN-FM-033 (Completion Report), EN-FM-034 (KPI Dashboard), EN-FM-035 (Quarterly Management Review Minutes), EN-FM-036 (Annual Department Compliance Attestation), EN-FM-037 (Enterprise Management Certification — Administrator + CFO).
11. **HR Leave / Accommodation:** Created HR-FM-040 (Leave Request FMLA/CFRA/PDL/ADA), HR-FM-041 (Return-to-Work), HR-FM-042 (Reasonable Accommodation ADA/FEHA).
12. **49 additional audit-required forms** spanning FN (ADR review, CMS-838 credit balance, refund, 60-day overpayment, extrapolation, quantification, self-disclosure, post-audit CAP, AR aging, bad-debt, charity care), HR (ADA interactive process, fitness-for-duty, complaint intake, investigations, WC, OSHA, separation, classification, wage-hour), and IT (mobile/BYOD, removable media, vulnerability, sanitization, change mgmt, vendor security, email security, phishing, physical/privacy, CCPA/CPRA). **All created** as audit-valid structured templates.

### Cross-System Finding

13. **Workflow-form cross-reference integrity:** Initial pass showed 49 workflow form-IDs with no matching library entry. After creation of 68 new forms, all 342 unique workflow refs resolve cleanly to live library entries (349 total) with physical `.txt` files (351 files in folder — 349 forms + 2 index/support files).

## 5. GLOBAL PATTERNS

### Systemic Weaknesses Identified (All Remediated)

**Pattern A — Committee Minutes Dilution:**
Pre-audit workflows relied on generic phrasing ("minutes," "committee approval") without mapping to a specific committee-minutes form. *Remediation:* Created dedicated minutes form per committee (GV, CO, QA, FN-Finance, FN-Audit, RM-Risk, RM-Safety, IT-Security, CAB) and embedded in every relevant workflow in Steps / Required Forms / Approvals / Outputs / Audit Requirements.

**Pattern B — Form ID Drift:**
Workflow authors referenced form IDs that exceeded the library's then-current range (e.g., HR-FM-040+ when library had only HR-FM-039). *Remediation:* Created 68 new forms as audit-valid structured templates filling every forward reference; Forms Library expanded from 281 → **349 forms**.

**Pattern C — Board-Reporting Asymmetry:**
Workflows routinely captured "send report to Board" without the corresponding GV-FM-005 capture of Board receipt / deliberation / vote. *Remediation:* GV-FM-005 now embedded in 199 workflow points spanning all 10 domains.

**Pattern D — Interim Substitution Debt:**
Early audit passes used `EN-FM-021 Inter-Domain Coordination Meeting Minutes` as an interim for missing committee minutes. *Remediation:* All interim substitutions replaced by dedicated committee-specific forms.

**Pattern E — Source P&P Update Debt:**
Source policies (`.docx`) were written before the new committee-minutes and forms infrastructure existed. *Remediation:* `PP_AMENDMENT_REGISTER.md` produced, enumerating every required P&P text insertion/clarification for the next republication cycle. Workflows already implement these requirements operationally.

**Pattern F — Out-of-Range Form IDs:** Resolved — all 49 previously-broken IDs now have live forms.

**Pattern G — Misnamed Form References:** Resolved — all mis-citations (CO-FM-003, GV-FM-010, GV-FM-011) corrected.

### Structural Issues — Status

- **Orphan processes:** NONE. Every workflow maps to at least one policy ID, and every workflow references forms actually in the library.
- **Broken dependencies:** NONE. 342 unique form references, 0 broken.
- **Version control:** Every new form is versioned (v1.0, effective 2026-04-21, next review 2027-04-21); forms index updated.
- **Evidence traceability:** Every workflow step that requires documentation now has a concrete form with a concrete form ID, owner, frequency, and retention.

---

### **SURVEY-READY**

**Justification:**
1. Workflows: 166 / 166 compliant with 13-section structure. No partial workflows.

6. **Stop condition met:** 3 consecutive full-system passes with ZERO issues.

# CL — CLINICAL OPERATIONS — WORKFLOWS

**Domain Code:** CL
**Regulatory Anchors:** 42 CFR § 484.45 (OASIS submission); § 484.50 (Patient Rights); § 484.55 (Comprehensive Assessment); § 484.60 (Plan of Care & coordination); § 484.65 (QAPI); § 484.70 (Infection Prevention); § 484.75 (Home Health Aide Services); § 484.80 (Aide Training/Competency/Supervision); § 484.110 (Clinical Records); § 484.115 (Personnel Qualifications); § 484.245 (HH QRP); Social Security Act § 1814(a)(2)(C) & § 1835(a)(2)(A) (Face-to-Face); CA H&S Code §1726 et seq.
**Primary Subdomains:** PA (Patient Assessment), CP (Care Planning & Coordination), OA (OASIS), SD (Service Delivery), IC (Infection Control), DC (Discharge)
**Form Prefix:** CL-FM-xxx (57 forms)

---

## DOMAIN OVERVIEW

Clinical workflows execute the day-to-day delivery of home health care. Every workflow is tied to a Medicare Condition of Participation and directly drives claim payability, quality outcomes, and patient safety. OASIS, POC, orders, face-to-face, and supervision workflows are simultaneously clinical, billing-compliance, and survey-defensibility processes. Any failure cascades into denials, False Claims Act exposure, and CoP deficiencies.

---

## WORKFLOWS IN THIS DOMAIN

1. CL-WF-01 — Intake & Referral Qualification
2. CL-WF-02 — Homebound Status Determination
3. CL-WF-03 — Face-to-Face Encounter Capture & Verification
4. CL-WF-04 — Start of Care (SOC) Comprehensive Assessment
5. CL-WF-05 — OASIS Completion, QA, Transmission & Correction
6. CL-WF-06 — Plan of Care (POC / CMS-485) Establishment & Physician Signature
7. CL-WF-07 — Physician Orders & Verbal Order Authentication
8. CL-WF-08 — Coordination of Care & Multidisciplinary Communication
9. CL-WF-09 — Skilled Visit Documentation (RN / PT / OT / SLP / MSW)
10. CL-WF-10 — Home Health Aide Services & Supervision (Skilled-Patient Annual; Aide-Only Semiannual)
11. CL-WF-11 — Annual Aide In-Service Training (≥12 hours)
12. CL-WF-12 — Medication Management & Reconciliation
13. CL-WF-13 — Wound Care & Specialty Clinical Protocols
14. CL-WF-14 — Infection Control at Point of Care
15. CL-WF-15 — Telehealth Service Delivery
16. CL-WF-16 — Patient Rights, Admission Consent & Advance Directives
17. CL-WF-17 — Patient / Family Education
18. CL-WF-18 — Recertification / Resumption of Care (ROC)
19. CL-WF-19 — Transfer / Discharge Planning & Execution
20. CL-WF-20 — Missed Visit Management
21. CL-WF-21 — Clinical Record Completion & Amendment
22. CL-WF-22 — Abuse / Neglect / Exploitation Reporting
23. CL-WF-23 — Patient Complaint / Grievance Handling
24. CL-WF-24 — Pediatric / Palliative / High-Risk Specialty Pathways
25. CL-WF-25 — Clinician Competency Validation (Incl. OASIS)

## CL-WF-01 — INTAKE & REFERRAL QUALIFICATION

### 1. POLICY REFERENCES
- CL-PA-001 Comprehensive Patient Assessment; OP-IN-001 Intake; GV-GB-001 (acceptance-to-service); 42 CFR § 484.60(a); § 484.105(i)(1)

### 2. PROCESS OVERVIEW
Receives referrals; verifies eligibility (physician order, homebound, skilled need, Medicare/insurance, geographic service area, clinical scope); accepts or declines; schedules SOC.

### 3. TRIGGER(S)
- Incoming referral (hospital, physician, community, patient, insurer)

### 4. RESPONSIBLE ROLES
- **Primary:** Intake Coordinator / Admissions Nurse
- **Supporting:** Clinical Manager, Insurance Verifier, Physician liaison
- **Approval:** Clinical Manager (acceptance decisions; non-admits)

### 5. INPUTS
- Referral form; H&P; hospital discharge summary; physician order to initiate; demographics; insurance

### 6. STEP-BY-STEP EXECUTION

| # | Action | Role | System Action | Form | Deadline |
|---|--------|------|---------------|------|----------|
| 1 | Log referral | Intake Coord | Referral log | CL-FM-050 Documentation Source Evidence Matrix (source log) | Within 4 business hours |
| 2 | Capture referral demographics & clinical summary | Intake Coord | Intake entry | CL-FM-050; OP-FM-014 Patient Intake Information Sheet | Same day |
| 3 | Verify Medicare/insurance, homebound, skilled need | Insurance Verifier + Admissions RN | Eligibility check | CL-FM-009 Homebound Status Determination Checklist | Same day |
| 4 | Verify physician order exists & is compliant | Intake Coord | Order verification | CL-FM-006 Physician Orders Sheet | Same day |
| 5 | Confirm scope against agency Acceptance-to-Service | Clinical Mgr | Scope check | GV-FM-016 Scope of Services Definition Matrix | Same day |
| 6 | Accept or decline | Clinical Mgr | Decision | OP-FM-015 Non-Admit / Referral Rejection Log (if declined) | Within 24h of referral |
| 7 | Schedule SOC | Scheduler | Visit scheduled | — | SOC within 48h of referral (or per physician order) |
| 8 | Notify referral source of acceptance/decline | Intake Coord | Notification | — | Within 24h of decision |
| 9 | Send intake packet to patient | Intake Coord | Packet delivery | CL-FM-027 Patient Rights & Responsibilities; CL-FM-029 Informed Consent | Prior to first visit |

### 7. REQUIRED FORMS & DOCUMENTS
CL-FM-050, CL-FM-009, CL-FM-006, CL-FM-027, CL-FM-029, OP-FM-014, OP-FM-015, GV-FM-016. Linguistics: CL-FM-025 Telehealth Consent (if applicable); OP-FM-018 Interpreter Service Utilization Log (if LEP).

### 8. APPROVALS
Clinical Manager approves acceptance decisions and all non-admits. Insurance Verifier certifies benefits.

### 9. OUTPUTS
Referral log, intake packet delivered, eligibility verification evidence, acceptance/decline record, scheduled SOC.

### 10. SLA / DEADLINES
SOC within 48 hours of referral (internal standard — unless ordered later by physician). Decline logged within 24h.

### 11. ESCALATION LOGIC
Incomplete referral → Intake Coord requests missing items; if not resolved within 24h, escalate to Clinical Manager. Out-of-scope referral → formal decline with referral back to appropriate provider; patient continuity of care documented.

### 12. FAILURE CONDITIONS
Accepting patient outside scope → adverse event, malpractice. Accepting without physician order → non-payable claim + False Claims Act exposure. Missing homebound/skilled need documentation at intake → claim denial.

### 13. AUDIT REQUIREMENTS
Per-referral file with: referral, eligibility checks, scope assessment, accept/decline decision, physician order. Non-admit log complete with rationale.

---

## CL-WF-02 — HOMEBOUND STATUS DETERMINATION

### 1. POLICY REFERENCES
- CL-PA-002 Homebound Eligibility; 42 CFR § 409.42; SSA § 1835(a)(2)(F)

### 2. PROCESS OVERVIEW
Establishes and re-establishes homebound status at SOC, at each recert, and when clinical status changes materially.

### 3. TRIGGER(S)
- SOC
- Recertification
- Significant clinical change
- Audit signal

### 4. RESPONSIBLE ROLES
- **Primary:** Admitting RN; Case Manager
- **Supporting:** Physician, Clinical Mgr
- **Approval:** Clinical Manager (quarterly spot-audit)

### 5. INPUTS
- Clinical findings; caregiver reports; physician orders

### 6. STEP-BY-STEP EXECUTION

| # | Action | Role | Form | Deadline |
|---|--------|------|------|----------|
| 1 | Complete homebound checklist at SOC | Admitting RN | CL-FM-009 Homebound Status Determination Checklist | At SOC |
| 2 | Document specific narrative (taxing effort, medical restriction) | Admitting RN | Chart note | At SOC |
| 3 | Re-verify at every recert | Recertifying clinician | CL-FM-009 | At recert |
| 4 | Escalate change in status (no longer homebound) → DC planning | Clinician | DC note | Same day |
| 5 | Quarterly audit sample | Clinical Mgr | Audit notes; CO-FM-021 Documentation Alignment Audit Tool | Quarterly |

### 7. REQUIRED FORMS & DOCUMENTS
CL-FM-009; CO-FM-021.

### 8. APPROVALS
Clinician attests; Clinical Manager audits.

### 9. OUTPUTS
Completed checklist in chart; narrative evidence; audit results.

### 10. SLA / DEADLINES
Every SOC, recert, material change.

### 11. ESCALATION LOGIC
No longer homebound → discharge planning initiated; billing stops until discharge; physician notified.

### 12. FAILURE CONDITIONS
Missing/weak homebound evidence = claim denial, False Claims Act signal for pattern.

### 13. AUDIT REQUIREMENTS
Each episode chart shows homebound documentation; audit log current.

---

## CL-WF-03 — FACE-TO-FACE ENCOUNTER CAPTURE & VERIFICATION

### 1. POLICY REFERENCES
- CL-PA-005 Face-to-Face Encounter; 42 CFR § 424.22(a)(1)(v); SSA § 1814(a)(2)(C); § 1835(a)(2)(A)

### 2. PROCESS OVERVIEW
Obtains and verifies the physician or allowed NPP face-to-face encounter documentation supporting Medicare HH eligibility.

### 3. TRIGGER(S)
- New Medicare SOC
- Episode with required F2F
- Audit / denial signal

### 4. RESPONSIBLE ROLES
- **Primary:** Intake/Clinical Liaison; Clinical Mgr
- **Supporting:** Physician, Billing

### 5. INPUTS
- F2F encounter note; physician certification; encounter date

### 6. STEP-BY-STEP EXECUTION

| # | Action | Role | Form | Deadline |
|---|--------|------|------|----------|
| 1 | Confirm F2F encounter within 90 days prior or 30 days after SOC | Intake/Liaison | CL-FM-010 Face-to-Face Encounter Documentation | Before billing |
| 2 | Validate content (date, clinical findings supporting HH, signed by physician/NPP) | Clinical Mgr | CL-FM-010 | Before billing |
| 3 | Obtain if missing (request from physician) | Liaison | Outreach log | Before billing |
| 4 | If unavailable/non-compliant: halt billing; evaluate non-billable / patient-responsibility | Billing/Compliance | CO-FM-021 | Before claim |
| 5 | Record in chart | Clinical Mgr | Chart | Before billing |

### 7. REQUIRED FORMS & DOCUMENTS
CL-FM-010; CO-FM-021.

### 8. APPROVALS
Clinical Manager attests completeness before billing release.

### 9. OUTPUTS
F2F encounter in chart; billing release signal.

### 10. SLA / DEADLINES
Completion before claim submission; no retroactive fabrication.

### 11. ESCALATION LOGIC
Non-compliant F2F → claim held; Compliance Officer informed; refund/denial process triggered if claim already submitted.

### 12. FAILURE CONDITIONS
Missing F2F = automatic Medicare denial + potential False Claims Act exposure if submitted.

### 13. AUDIT REQUIREMENTS
F2F in every Medicare-billed chart; pre-bill edit evidence.

## CL-WF-04 — START OF CARE (SOC) COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENT

### 1. POLICY REFERENCES
- CL-PA-001; CL-OA-001 OASIS; 42 CFR § 484.55, § 484.60(a); § 484.45

### 2. PROCESS OVERVIEW
Completes the comprehensive assessment (incl. OASIS) at SOC within 48 hours of referral (or as ordered by physician).

### 3. TRIGGER(S)
- Scheduled SOC visit

### 4. RESPONSIBLE ROLES
- **Primary:** Admitting RN (or PT for therapy-only case under state scope)
- **Supporting:** Disciplines for specialty components
- **Approval:** Clinical Manager

### 5. INPUTS
- Referral packet; F2F encounter; prior records; medications

### 6. STEP-BY-STEP EXECUTION

| # | Action | Role | Form | Deadline |
|---|--------|------|------|----------|
| 1 | Perform SOC visit; complete assessment | Admitting RN | CL-FM-001 Start of Care (SOC) Comprehensive Assessment | Within 48h of referral (or per order) |
| 2 | Complete OASIS-E1 | Admitting RN | CL-FM-002 OASIS-E1 Assessment Form | Day of SOC |
| 3 | Complete Homebound Determination (CL-WF-02) | RN | CL-FM-009 | Day of SOC |
| 4 | Capture fall risk, pain, cognitive, behavioral, functional | RN | CL-FM-020 Fall Risk Assessment Tool; CL-FM-026 Pain Assessment Scale; CL-FM-038 Behavioral Health Screening Tool | Day of SOC |
| 5 | Medication reconciliation (CL-WF-12) | RN | CL-FM-019 | Day of SOC |
| 6 | Obtain consents & patient rights acknowledgment (CL-WF-16) | RN | CL-FM-027 Patient Rights; CL-FM-029 Informed Consent | Day of SOC |
| 7 | Develop initial POC (CL-WF-06) | RN | CL-FM-005 Plan of Care (485) | Within 5 days of SOC (CoP) |
| 8 | Submit assessment for QA (CL-WF-05) | QA Reviewer | CL-FM-031 OASIS Pre-Submission QA Checklist | Within 7 days of SOC |

### 7. REQUIRED FORMS & DOCUMENTS
CL-FM-001, CL-FM-002, CL-FM-009, CL-FM-019, CL-FM-020, CL-FM-026, CL-FM-027, CL-FM-029, CL-FM-038, CL-FM-005, CL-FM-031. Specialty: CL-FM-039 Pediatric; CL-FM-041 MSW; CL-FM-047 High-Risk.

### 8. APPROVALS
Clinical Manager reviews; QA reviewer signs OASIS QA; Physician signs POC.

### 9. OUTPUTS
Complete SOC assessment packet; OASIS; initial POC; signed consents.

### 10. SLA / DEADLINES
SOC within 48h of referral (best practice) or per physician order. OASIS within 5 days of SOC (CoP). POC within 5 days; physician signature within 30 days.

### 11. ESCALATION LOGIC
SOC delay → Scheduler + Clinical Mgr notified immediately; new scheduled date; documented rationale in chart.

### 12. FAILURE CONDITIONS
Missing/late SOC = CoP deficiency; claim payment risk. OASIS errors → claim denial, quality measure impact.

### 13. AUDIT REQUIREMENTS
Per-chart: SOC note, OASIS, POC, consents, F2F, homebound, meds — all timestamped.
